newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - March 3.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - March 3.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian cricket players Greg Blewett and Steve Waugh launched a planned attack on South African spinner Paul Adams as part of Australia's attempt to take control of the competition, on the third day of the first test of the South African tour. Page 25.

Australian golfer Karrie Webb has lost the Alpine Ladies Masters at Royal Pines on the Gold Coast. She squandered a five-shot lead during the last round of the tournament losing to Canadian Gail Graham. Webb was clearly devastated by the unexpected loss. Page 27.

Increasing controversy is surrounding the choice of Rushcutters Bay, Sydney, as the venue for the 2000 Olympic regatta. A number of other options around Sydney are being canvassed including the nearby Garden Island naval base and the park surrounding Woolahra Sailing Club on the shores of Rose Bay. Page 26.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The launch of the Super League competition on the weekend showed that despite all the hype it is still old fashioned football. The four games played on the weekend demonstrated however that it is also a made-for-TV sport with emphasis being placed on offield entertainment and referee-spectator involvement. Page 25.

In what proved to be the race of the champions, Melinda Gainsford-Taylor beat old rival Cathy Freeman in the 200m title at the national titles in Melbourne yesterday. Gainsford-Taylor set a time of 22.34s with a five-metre tail wind. Page 26.

Sydney high school teacher Debbie Sosimenko set a Commonwealth record at the national championships on the weekend in the women's hammer with a throw of 65.68m. The record breaks her old mark set two years ago by 1.5m. The women's hammer throw is eamarked for inclusion for the first time in the 2000 Olympics. Page 26.
THE AGE

Australian Football League club Carlton ensured an Ansett Cup semi-final against either North Melbourne or Richmond with a 28 point win against Adelaide at Football Park last night. The win broke Adelaide's recent string of victories with their new coach Malcolm Blight. Page 2.

The Australian cricket team has chosen its new No 3 batsman to replace the legendary David Boon. The place has been awarded to Matthew Elliott who scored 85 runs from 113 balls in the first Test match against South Africa yesterday. Elliott has consistently looked like Australia's best batsman on the South African tour. Page 6.

Scott Petersen is jubilant following his win in the 1500 metres finals at the Australian National Championships on the weekend. The win is a culmination of a troubled career filled with setbacks which include Petersen's fall in the 1500 metres final two year ago and finishing last in the 1993 junior race. Page 10.
THE HERALD SUN

The Australian Football League commission is considering increasing the number of general admission tickets to the Docklands stadium in Melbourne. The move follows concerns that proposed new stadium ticket prices would be too high. Under the proposal 16000 $A12.50 seats could become available in the 52,000 seat venue. Page 76.

Australian Tim Forsyth set a new Australian record in the high jump at the national championships this weekend. Forsyth, who won bronze at the Barcelona Olympics, recovered from a four year career slump to set a 2.36m record at his third attempt. The win breaks the previous Australian record of 2.35m which he set at a grand prix meeting in Canberra in 1993. Page 78.

Sprinter Stephen Brimacombe is today struggling with his disappointment after being forced to withdraw from a trip to Paris because of a tooth infection. Brimacombe was already sick with the infection when he ran in the 100m and 200m events in the nationl championships on the weekend. Despite this he won the former event and came second in the latter. Page 78. --
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Super League referee Bill Harrigan wants the controversial "wired for sound" microphone innovation scrapped. His voice was clearly heard in thousands of viewers homes on free-to-air TV coverage of the Super League's gala launch match on Saturday night. Viewer reaction to the microphone coverage has been mixed. Page 27.

Super League player Ryan Girdler is being considered as a member of the Australian side to play New Zealand Anzac Day test match. Girdler has impressed selectors recently with his skilful playing and ability to withstand injury. Page 31.

The Australian national soccer competition, the Ericsson Cup, was enlivened by a match between UTS Olympic and Sydney United on Sunday night. In a controversial last minute penalty play off, UTS Olympic scored to make it a 1-1 draw. Page 42.
